candidates: In diagram rendering and utility code, use `log.debug()` or `log.trace()` for development debugging statements rather than `log.info()` or `log.warn()`; remove or reduce excessively chatty debug logging before merging.
Remove unused variables, function parameters, imports, exported types/functions, and commented-out code blocks before merging; do not leave dead code in the codebase.

Verify that developer scratch HTML files, backup files (e.g. `*-old.md`), generated temp files (e.g. Vite timestamp `.mjs` files), unused asset files, and work-in-progress files from unrelated features have not been accidentally committed.

Ensure variable and parameter names accurately describe their purpose (e.g. `siblingWidth`/`siblingHeight` instead of `w`/`h`, `radius` not `radious`); also avoid shadowing outer-scope variable names with same-named inner-scope variables.

Diagram renderers and layout functions must read runtime settings (e.g. `padding`, `useMaxWidth`) from the diagram's own config section via `configApi.getConfig().<diagramName>` rather than hardcoding values; this applies to every call site where a config-controllable value appears.

Keep JSDoc `@param` descriptions, `@example` blocks, and prose accurate and up-to-date; flag stale or copy-pasted doc blocks that describe a different function, wrong parameter names, or incorrect behavior.

Do not use module-level mutable variables (e.g. `let minX = 0` at the top of a file) in diagram rendering or layout modules; refactor them into function-local variables or return them from the function to prevent state leakage across parallel diagram renders.
Prefer early `return` or `continue` statements over deeply nested if-else chains; if-return ladders are easier to read and maintain than multiple levels of indentation.

Prefer `{ ...obj }` (shallow) or `structuredClone(obj)` (deep) instead of `lodash.clone()` / `lodash.cloneDeep()` when copying objects to avoid unnecessary bundle size; note that `structuredClone` requires browsers from 2022+.

Do not use the `I` prefix naming convention for TypeScript interface or type alias names (e.g. use `GenerateId` not `IGenerateId`); derive complex types with `typeof` or mapped types rather than manually writing parallel interface declarations.

Define diagram DB modules using the `const db = { ... } as const` export pattern so that TypeScript infers the DB type automatically (e.g. `export type BlockDB = typeof db & DiagramDB`), eliminating the need for manually written `IFunctionName`-style type declarations.

When a type is already defined in the project's canonical config type file (`config.type.ts`), re-export it from there instead of duplicating the definition in a diagram-local file (e.g. `export type { BlockDiagramConfig as BlockConfig } from '../../config.type.js'`).

In diagram rendering code, type D3 containers and groups with specific generic parameters using the project's `Group` type from `diagram-api/types.ts` rather than using `ContainerElement`, `any`, or `unknown`.
Do not wrap functions in `try...catch` unless they can actually throw; also remove `any` casts that exist only to suppress TypeScript errors caused by incorrect type annotations elsewhere.
Do not insert blank lines between import statements within an import block; blank lines within import blocks can interfere with auto-sort tooling and create noisy diffs.
When adding a `styles.ts` file for a new diagram type, add a corresponding test case in `packages/mermaid/src/styles.spec.ts` to verify the style function.

When adding a new diagram config section to `config.schema.yaml`, do not explicitly redeclare defaults (e.g. `useMaxWidth`) that are already defined and inherited from `BaseDiagramConfig`; only add properties specific to the new diagram.
In `config.schema.yaml`, every new property entry must include an explicit `type:` field (e.g. `type: number`) alongside any `default` value.

Do not include jison grammar rules for syntax features that are not yet implemented or supported in the diagram type; remove placeholder rules and track planned features elsewhere (e.g. in an issue or a TODO comment).

Keep Mermaid diagram code examples in documentation consistent with surrounding prose descriptions; when the text says "block b spans two columns," the example must actually demonstrate that behavior, and incorrect or misleading descriptions must be corrected.

Documentation for a new diagram type must cover all supported syntax features with usage examples, including non-obvious ones (e.g. `columns auto`, `space:N`, `%%` comments); remove duplicate sections that repeat content already covered elsewhere in the same document.

When duplicating a function that already exists in another diagram module, add a `// TODO:` or `@privateRemarks TODO:` comment noting the duplication and the intended consolidation point to prevent silent drift between the copies.

Verify that all Mermaid diagram strings used as fixtures in Cypress and unit tests are syntactically valid (e.g. no unclosed string literals, correct token separation such as closing parentheses before `:N` width specifiers) to prevent false test failures.

New helper, utility, and diagram implementation files added to the project must use the `.ts` extension and be fully typed rather than being added as `.js` files; TypeScript types improve maintainability and catch errors at compile time.
